text: Got it — investigating the required-flag bug in src/click/core.py now. ETA ~10 minutes.

`click.prompt` catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and `EOFError` internally and re-raises `click.Abort` (src/click/termui.py, lines 144-150). So callers see `Abort`, not the original exception — `confirm` and `pause` do the same. This is documented in the `prompt` docstring ("If the user aborts the input by sending an interrupt signal this function will catch it and raise a :exc:`Abort` exception") and in docs/exceptions.rst.

If the `locale.getpreferredencoding()` lookup (or the `codecs.lookup` of its result) raises, the `except Exception` branch sets `fs_enc = "ascii"` (src/click/_unicodefun.py, line 13). That then triggers the ASCII-environment check and the `RuntimeError` with the mitigation hints.
On it — the None-stream bug across _compat.py/_termui_impl.py/utils.py. ETA ~12 minutes.

`RuntimeError` — `_verify_python_env` ends with `raise RuntimeError("\n\n".join(extra))` (src/click/_unicodefun.py, line 100). The `extra` list holds the "Click will abort further execution because Python was configured to use ASCII as encoding" message plus locale hints.

It returns the sentinel `_flag_needs_value` (src/click/parser.py, lines 466-469) — i.e. the option is recorded as present with no value, so the higher-level `Option` can then fall back to its `flag_value`/default. If `_flag_needs_value` were false it would instead raise `BadOptionUsage` ("Option {name!r} requires an argument.").
On it — the envvar/flag_value bug in src/click/core.py. ETA ~12 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: in `Option.__init__` (src/click/core.py), any flag with no explicit `default` was unconditionally given `self.default = False` — even when `required=True`. So `get_default()` returned `False`, `value_is_missing(False)` was False, and the `MissingParameter` branch was skipped; the command ran with exit code 0. Fix: `if is_flag and default_is_missing and not self.required:` so a required flag keeps `default=None` and raises `Missing option '--flag'.` (exit 2). Verified: reproduction now exits 2 with the proper usage error, and the full suite is unchanged (488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed, no pre-existing failures).
`TypeError`: `style` wraps `_interpret_color(fg)` in `try/except KeyError` and re-raises as `TypeError(f"Unknown color {fg!r}")` (src/click/termui.py, lines 580-584). Same for `bg` (lines 586-590).
From `click.utils`: `from .utils import echo as echo` (src/click/__init__.py, line 67).
On it — the cls-preservation bug in src/click/decorators.py. ETA ~12 minutes.

Fixed. Root cause: when `sys.stdout`/`sys.stderr` are `None`, `_make_cached_stream_func` (src/click/_compat.py) returned `None` from `_default_text_stdout()`/`_default_text_stderr()`, and nothing downstream handled it — `utils.echo` crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'write'`, as did `pager` and `ProgressBar`. Fixes: (1) `_compat._make_cached_stream_func` returns `None` early when the source stream is None; (2) `utils.echo` returns silently when the resolved stream is None; (3) `_termui_impl.pager`/`ProgressBar` fall back to `io.StringIO()`. Verified: echo/secho/pager/progressbar no longer raise with None streams, and the full suite is unchanged (488 passed, 21 skipped, 1 xfailed).

It returns `"Invalid value: {message}"` (src/click/exceptions.py, line 120) — i.e. `Invalid value: <message>`, with no parameter hint. Otherwise it returns `"Invalid value for {param_hint}: {message}"`, using `self.param_hint` if set, else `self.param.get_error_hint(self.ctx)`.
#1 is fixed and verified (required flags now raise MissingParameter; full suite unchanged).
#4 is fixed and verified (None stdout/stderr no longer crash echo/pager/ProgressBar; full suite unchanged).

It returns the items joined with `" / "`, each wrapped in `repr()`: `" / ".join(repr(x) for x in param_hint)` (src/click/exceptions.py, lines 17-18). For a string (or None) it just returns `param_hint` unchanged.
